provenance.notes: Out family batch, book archetype. Low ticket, pure recurring revenue: the kit leans on weekly routes, visit reports, autopay and green-pool rescues, with prices sized for a route business. Standard direction is C47, not C39. No chemical or equipment brands named. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.section: What happens on a weekly pool visit
pageStructurePlus.contains: Skimming, brushing, vacuuming, emptying baskets, testing and balancing chemicals, checking the filter pressure, and the visit report with readings sent after every stop
pageStructurePlus.why: Pool owners can't see what the tech did while they were at work. A visit checklist and report is what keeps them paying monthly.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Algae clean-ups, shock and filter cleaning, when a drain and clean is needed, how many visits it takes, and the switch to weekly service afterwards
pageStructurePlus.why: A green pool is an urgent, embarrassing problem and the most common first job. It turns into a weekly customer.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Spring opening, cover removal and start-up, autumn closing, winterising lines, and booking windows for each
pageStructurePlus.why: In seasonal climates, openings and closings are the two booking rushes of the year. A page that books them fills the route.

pageStructurePlus.section: Pump, filter, heater and salt cell repair
pageStructurePlus.contains: Noisy pumps, leaking filters, heaters that won't light, salt cells that need cleaning, leak detection, and replacing equipment
pageStructurePlus.why: Equipment repair is where a pool cleaning route earns real money. Owners want to know their weekly tech can fix it too.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Which neighbourhoods are served on which days, how quickly a new pool can start, and a waitlist sign-up for full routes
pageStructurePlus.why: Pool routes are built on density. Showing service days by neighbourhood sells the street and lets owners join when there's room.

designDirections.name: Clear by Friday
designDirections.bestFor: Solo pool techs building a route who need a price, a green-pool offer and a sign-up
designDirections.headlineSample: Pool cleaning in {City}, weekly or one-time
designDirections.whyItFits: Sky blue reads as clear water, and the soft rounded type feels like a friendly neighbour tech rather than a company.

designDirections.name: Weekly Route
designDirections.bestFor: Pool service companies selling weekly plans, openings, closings and repairs by route
designDirections.whyItFits: Not the family's brick-and-linen combo, which reads masonry and heritage: teal reads as clean pool water and the humanist type suits a friendly booking page.

designDirections.name: Community Pools
designDirections.bestFor: Pool service firms bidding HOA, apartment and hotel pools with logs and inspections
designDirections.headlineSample: Commercial pool service for {City} HOAs and properties
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a neutral grotesque read like a facilities proposal, which is how managers compare commercial pool contractors.

openers.line: A new homeowner in {City} with a pool they don't know how to look after searches for pool service and finds {Business Name} with no site. They want a monthly price and a way to start.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there's no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: What a new pool owner would find instead: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing goes to Facebook, where the green-to-blue pool from last week is your best ad and it's already buried. Someone with a green pool wants to book a rescue, not scroll.
openers.hook: Tap the link and confirm it goes to Facebook. Note any green-to-clean post.
openers.linkLine: A pool service page with booking: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your site still lists an old monthly pool cleaning price and a form that doesn't send. In a route business, a broken sign-up is a lost customer every week.
openers.hook: Open the site, try the form, and check prices and the year. Note what's broken.
openers.linkLine: Same pool service, with a sign-up that works: {demo-link}

openers.line: On a phone your pool service site's book button sits under a pop-up that won't close. Owners look up pool help standing at the edge of a cloudy pool.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on a phone and note what breaks. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your pool booking, working on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to book weekly pool service or a green pool clean-up with {Business Name} online. Most owners would pick a start date, enter the gate code and pay on file in a minute.
openers.hook: Check listing, bios and any site for booking. If calling is the only path, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: Online booking for weekly pool service and rescues: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your green-to-blue pool posts are the most convincing thing a pool tech can share. They scroll away instead of sitting on a rescue page that books the next one.
openers.hook: Find a green-to-clean before-and-after they posted. Mention it if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your pool rescues, on a page that books the next one: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your reviews mention a tech who sends readings after every visit and a pool that's never been cloudy since. That's why people stay with a pool service, and it's stuck on your listing.
openers.hook: Copy one review phrase about reliability or reports. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those reviews next to your weekly service plans: {demo-link}

openers.line: When covers come off in spring, every owner with a green surprise underneath calls a pool service the same week. Being bookable online that week fills the route for the summer.
openers.hook: Use in late winter for openings, late summer for closings, or before peak season in warm climates. Name the timing.

openers.line: Pools turn cloudy on the weekend right before the party. A pool service booking that works on Saturday catches that owner before they try to fix it with the wrong chemicals.
openers.hook: Call their number on a weekend. If it hits voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A pool service request that works on weekends: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring a pool tech. Good techs look for a company that seems organised and has a full route.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring note. Note the date.
openers.linkLine: A pool service site with a careers page: {demo-link}

openers.line: You already service pools in a few neighbourhoods, but nothing tells someone in {Neighborhood} you're on their street on Thursdays. Density is everything for a pool route.
openers.hook: Find neighbourhoods named in reviews or posts; use one where they clearly have customers.
openers.linkLine: A pool service page for each route neighbourhood: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer pool service on monthly autopay, say so on the booking page. Owners like one flat number and never thinking about chemicals again.
openers.hook: Only if they mention monthly plans or autopay. Otherwise skip.

openers.line: Some states license pool work, and every owner worries about a tech in the backyard with the kids' toys. Your licence and insurance on the site settle that.
openers.hook: Check the state registry if pool service is licensed there. Never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and techs on one pool page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Pool owners talk to other pool owners at every barbecue. When they recommend you, there's nowhere for their friend to book.
openers.hook: Look for reviews mentioning friends or neighbours. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where the next pool service referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a great pool rescue, swamp to sparkling. That should be the first thing a stranger sees.
openers.hook: Pick their newest rescue, repair or opening post and name it, town if tagged.
openers.linkLine: That pool job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hi {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a great pool rescue.

I was looking for pool service in {City} and found {Business Name} on Maps, but no site where an owner can see your weekly plan and book a start date. I built a sample pool service site with online booking, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case this got buried. Here's the sample pool service site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has weekly plans with online booking and autopay, a green pool rescue page, and visit reports explained. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave it.

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, then ask how many more pools they want on the route
"It's {Build Range} depending on how many booking types and neighbourhood pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For your route I'd quote about {Build Price}. A few new weekly pools covers it."
"Ten minutes this week to look at it together?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a short scope and a deposit invoice. It's live before opening season."

objections.handler: "Then the waitlist and neighbourhood pages help you add pools only on streets you already drive, and raise prices on the far ones."

objections.objection: Pool service is word of mouth.
objections.handler: "It is. Friends still look you up before booking, and right now they can't book. The site turns a recommendation into a start date."

objections.objection: I can't afford a big website.
objections.handler: "It's sized for a pool route. A few new weekly pools pays for it, and the booking and autopay save you hours a week."

objections.objection: My customers like to text me.
objections.handler: "They still can. The site handles new sign-ups, rescues and openings so your texts are just your regulars."

objections.objection: I'm on a lead app already.
objections.handler: "Those pool leads go to several techs at once. Your own booking page sends the owner straight to your route."
"{Build Range}. For you about {Build Price}: weekly plans, booking, a rescue page and neighbourhood pages."

email.subject: Pool service site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for pool service companies in {City} and made a sample one for {Business Name} with online booking. I'll text the link. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm draining the {Business Name} pool service demo on Friday.

Want it kept up? Just a yes or no.

Hi {Owner}, opening season is close and the green-pool calls are about to start. Thought of {Business Name}.

The sample pool service site is still up, same price: {demo-link}

bullets: Size the build to the route: a few new weekly pools should pay for it in the first season.
Online booking with gate code, pool size and autopay is the core; never cut it.
Price the green pool rescue page separately; it is the most common first job and converts to weekly service.
Keep monthly products in tens of dollars; this owner bills in monthly pool plans.
Add the commercial pool page only for firms that want HOA or apartment contracts.
Neighbourhood pages are cheap and match how pool routes are built; sell them one at a time.

lineItems.description: Max with pool size and type, gate code, equipment notes, start date and card-on-file sign-up.

lineItems.item: Green pool rescue page with booking
lineItems.description: Max with before-and-after sets, a picture upload and a rescue-to-weekly offer.
Max with booking windows by week and a cover type field.
Max with a symptom picker for pumps, filters and heaters and a picture upload.
Max when each page shows the service day and a waitlist sign-up.
Max with sample chemical logs, inspection notes and a bid request form.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile upkeep for the pool route
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A green-to-blue rescue or a sparkling weekly pool goes on your Maps profile each week with the neighbourhood named."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review asks after the third clean visit
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "After a new customer's third weekly pool visit, when the water has stayed clear, they get a text asking for a review."

whatElseYouSell.name: Route-street door hangers
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Houses with pools on streets you already service get a door hanger: 'We clean pools on your street every Thursday.'"

whatElseYouSell.name: Opening season campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A campaign as covers come off offers openings and a first month of weekly pool service, aimed at your route neighbourhoods."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in February, run March to May.

whatElseYouSell.name: Truck magnet and decal artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Your truck parks in a pool owner's driveway every week. A decal with the booking site turns each stop into a sign for the street."

whatElseYouSell.name: New-owner pool guide
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A short printed and online guide for people who just bought a house with a pool, handed out by realtors, with your weekly plan inside."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 3, once there's a realtor to hand it out.

withoutAI.route: Pool builders who hand off after start-up
withoutAI.whoPays: The pool builder, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every new pool needs weekly service. The pool builder who sends you owners needs a site, and you send them remodel leads."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Service techs see every aging pool; builders hand off every new one.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "The supply store you buy chemicals from has DIY customers asking for help every day. A site with a pro referral page helps both."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Stores have budgets and want a service partner for owners who give up on DIY.

withoutAI.route: Pool leak detection and resurfacing specialists
withoutAI.whoPays: The specialist, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The leak detection tech you call when water levels drop needs a booking site. They'll send weekly service your way."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Specialists depend on route techs for referrals.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Listings with a green pool sell slower. A vendor page for pool homes puts your weekly service on the agent's list."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Agents refer vendors constantly and every pool home needs service.

withoutAI.route: Pest control and lawn companies on the same routes
withoutAI.whoPays: The pest or lawn company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The pest and lawn crews visit the same backyards on a schedule too. Swap referrals and both routes get denser."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Route businesses share neighbourhoods and the same buyer.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Rental managers need pools perfect before every check-in. A vendor booking page tied to turnovers keeps your pool service on their list."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Managers have many pools and pay for reliability.

withAI.route: Water test advice assistant for the supply store
withAI.pitchLine: "DIY owners enter test readings and get plain dosing advice, with an offer for weekly pool service when they're in over their heads."
withAI.whyItWorks: The store sells chemicals and your client gets the owners who give up.

withAI.route: Turnover-ready checks for vacation rental managers
withAI.pitchLine: "Before each guest arrives, the manager gets the latest pool reading and a clear-water picture from the tech, with any issue flagged."
withAI.whyItWorks: Bad pool reviews cost managers bookings; the pool client becomes indispensable.

withAI.route: Leak symptom checker for the leak detection specialist
withAI.pitchLine: "Owners describe how fast the water drops and whether it stops below the skimmer, and the assistant books a leak test when it looks real."
withAI.whyItWorks: Fewer wasted trips for the specialist, and leads flow both ways.

withAI.route: Pool home buyer briefing for realtors
withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers of a house with a pool get a short plain-language briefing on upkeep and a weekly service offer, branded for the agent."
withAI.whyItWorks: Agents look helpful; the pool client gets new owners at move-in.

withAI.route: Remodel lead flagging for the pool builder
withAI.pitchLine: "Route techs snap cracked plaster or loose tile; the assistant drafts a remodel lead for the builder with the owner's okay."
withAI.whyItWorks: Builders get warm remodel leads and send new pools back.

withAI.route: HOA pool log and inspection prep
withAI.pitchLine: "Community pool readings are logged every visit and the assistant flags anything a health inspector would question."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers fear failed inspections and closures; the pool client keeps the contract.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back with pool booking link
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Elbow-deep in a skimmer, you miss the call. The caller gets a text with your weekly pool service booking link and a rescue option if it's green."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their number forwarded and approved wording.

softwareAI.name: Monthly autopay for pool plans
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every weekly pool customer is billed on the first of the month on the card on file. Chemicals and parts are added automatically."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 1. Needs their payment account and plan prices.

softwareAI.name: Visit report with chemical readings
softwareAI.pitchLine: "After every stop, the owner gets the readings, what was added, a picture of the clear pool and any equipment notes."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their checklist and techs willing to tap through it.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts for pool customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New reviews about your pool techs get a short thank-you drafted in your voice, which you okay between stops."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs ten past replies. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Route optimiser for weekly stops
softwareAI.pitchLine: "New pools slot onto the right service day by street and the day's stops are ordered by drive time."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs current routes and tech start points.

softwareAI.name: Green pool picture triage
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners upload a picture of the pool and the tool sorts it into a quick clean, a full rescue or a drain and clean, with a price range for you to confirm."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs past rescue pictures labelled with what it took. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Skipped-visit and storm notices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a storm or a locked gate means a skipped pool visit, the owner gets a text with the reason and the make-up day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs the visit report in use.

softwareAI.name: Pool care chatbot
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'why is my water cloudy after a party' and 'can I swim after you shock it' from your own guidance, and books a visit if needed."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their answers written once. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Equipment record per pool
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each pool's pump, filter, heater and salt cell are recorded with ages and last service, so repair quotes are fast and accurate."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs techs logging equipment on their next visit.

softwareAI.name: Equipment age replacement offers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a pump or heater on file reaches the age where it usually fails, the owner gets a replacement quote before it dies on a hot weekend."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the equipment records.

softwareAI.name: Dosing helper for techs in the field
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The tech enters readings and pool volume and gets a dosing suggestion from the company's own rules, so new techs don't overshock."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their dosing rules and pool volumes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with reports and invoices
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Owners see every visit report, invoice and upcoming pool service day, and update their card or gate code themselves."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs autopay and visit reports in place.

softwareAI.name: After-hours pool service line
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Evening callers get help: what to do about a tripped pump tonight, and a repair or rescue booked for tomorrow."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their overnight advice and calendar. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Opening and closing scheduler
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Openings and closings fill week by week by neighbourhood, with cover type and equipment noted, so the rush runs in order."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, before the season. Needs their capacity per week.

softwareAI.name: Weekly route summary for the owner
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every Friday: pools serviced, problem pools, repair quotes sent, chemical spend, and which route has room for new pools."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs visit reports in use. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Chemical cost per pool tracker
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which pools use the most chemicals and time, so you reprice the ones losing money."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 8. Needs a season of visit reports.

softwareAI.name: Repair quote builder from visit notes
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a tech ticks leaking filter or noisy pump on the pool visit report, a repair quote with parts and labour is built from your price list for you to send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs their parts and labour price list and visit reports in use.

softwareAI.name: Commercial pool chemical log
softwareAI.pitchLine: "HOA and apartment pools get the daily or weekly chemical log health inspectors ask for, filled from each visit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 9, once they service commercial pools. Needs the local log requirements.

softwareAI.name: Referral reward messages
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Happy pool customers get a personal note offering a free month for each neighbour who signs up, written in your voice."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their referral offer. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Route tech hiring chat
softwareAI.pitchLine: "People asking about the pool tech job answer a few questions about driving record, heat and chemical handling, and the good ones get a ride-along booked."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Whenever they hire. Needs their requirements. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Pool route booking and reports as a subscription
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Solo pool techs all need booking, autopay and visit reports. Sell the bundle monthly to every route operator in the region."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Low price, many operators, identical workflow.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Pro referral network for a pool supply chain
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The pool supply chain or distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "DIY pool owners who give up need a pro. A referral network of service techs who buy from your stores keeps both sides loyal."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chains want to keep the chemical sale when owners switch to a pro.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Members switch on weekly plan booking, a green pool rescue page and visit reports as a membership perk."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Route operators are most of the membership and the least online.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Agency template for pool service clients
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Pool route clients can't pay for custom sites. A ready booking-first pool template makes them profitable for an agency."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Turns small clients into viable ones.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The pool service franchise, per territory
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each pool franchise owner gets local booking with their own route days, instead of a national form that loses the lead."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Territory owners pay for local sign-ups.

routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The vacation rental management company, annually
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every rental pool in your portfolio gets turnover-timed service and readings in one dashboard, from one pool contractor."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Managers with many pools buy once and roll it out.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: County health department pool log submission
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Public and community pools submit chemical logs online instead of on paper, and inspectors see problem pools first."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Health departments run inspections on paper and want cleaner data.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Every community pool you manage gets visit reports, chemical logs and repair approvals from one service provider."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Large portfolios buy once and value inspection-ready records.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Pool equipment claims need a vetted local tech fast. A dispatch page for approved pool service techs speeds every claim."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Warranty companies need reliable local techs and clean claim records.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Monthly chemical price note for pool techs
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Chlorine spikes wreck a flat monthly pool price. Techs who send in their supply receipts get a short sheet showing what everyone else is paying."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Chemical costs swing and techs underprice; contributed data keeps it honest.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: A pool route owner in the next metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A pool service company in another metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Pool routes live on density. I give one pool service per metro the booking, autopay and report stack, so you're not competing with my other client."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Same stack, new territory, no conflict.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Fix pool service sites with dead booking
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: The pool service with a broken site
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "If your pool site's booking form hasn't sent a message in months, I can move you onto a booking build that's working today."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Cheap, fast and the problem is obvious.

upsellLadder.offer: Pool service site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The pool service site and care plan go on one contract, so changing plan prices is a text to me."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first online sign-up, or they mention chasing a late payment.
upsellLadder.line: "Your first online pool customer is in. Let's put them on autopay before the first visit."

upsellLadder.offer: Review asks and Google profile upkeep
upsellLadder.trigger: New customers from the site have had three clear-water visits.
upsellLadder.line: "Three clean visits in, those pool owners are happy. Now's when to ask for reviews."

upsellLadder.trigger: A customer asks what the tech actually did, or questions a chemical charge.
upsellLadder.line: "That 'did you even come' message is what a pool visit report ends. Readings and a picture after every stop."

upsellLadder.trigger: New sign-ups land on streets off the current routes, or they add a second tech.
upsellLadder.line: "New pools are coming from all over. The optimiser puts each one on the right service day by street."

upsellLadder.trigger: A repair job needed a second trip because nobody knew the pump model.
upsellLadder.line: "That second trip for the right pump part is why every pool needs its equipment on file."

upsellLadder.trigger: Equipment records show a batch of pumps and heaters near the age they usually fail.
upsellLadder.line: "A dozen pumps on your route are getting old. Offering replacements before they fail is the best repair work there is."
